NEW DELHI: Delhi Police on Tuesday registered four FIRs over allegedly fake online posts circulated since October 10, while social media handles based in Pakistan remain under scrutiny as part of the investigation, news agency PTI reported."Till now, around 500 social media posts have been taken down that were spreading rumours or trying to create unrest among people," Delhi Police sources told news agency ANIOctober 10 was the scheduled date for a protest by the youth-led pressure group Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), which had planned to demand the resignation of chief election commission er Gyanesh Kumar over the Election Commission's conduct of the special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.However, a crackdown by the Centre largely curtailed the protest, with more than 7,000 people detained across Delhi.Those detained included members of the CJP's core team and several political leaders, among them four former chief ministers: Arvind Kejriwal, Mamata Banerjee, Pinarayi Vijayan and Manik Sarkar.

Article Title: Same cause, separate protests: Why Congress and CJP are keeping their distance
Article Text:
Protests by INDIA bloc and CJP over alleged voter-list manipulation and the Election Commission

Neha Bora joins Congress protest march to Supreme Court

A fight for political space?

Anti-CEC protest on two different days (left) Rahul, Priyanka getting detained on October 7; (right) CJP's Dipke, Das and Ranka getting detained on October 10

NEET protests showed similar pattern

(Left) NEET protest on July 20 by CJP; (right) anti-paper leak protest by Congress July 21

Rahul Gandhi said there are 'no parallel protests'

Assam episode brings differences into focus

Why did the Left, TMC and AAP join?

Pinarayi Vijayan, Mamata Banerjee, Arvind Kejriwal getting detained during October 10 protest

The Anna Hazare lesson

Anna Hazare, Arvind Kejriwal, Kiran Bedi during India Against Andolan movement, 2011

NEW DELHI: "All the protests are one protest," Rahul Gandhi said when asked about the parallel demonstrations against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Yet, despite their common demands, the Congress leader and the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leadership have not shared a stage.Congress and other INDIA bloc leaders on Monday marched towards the Supreme Court over alleged electoral irregularities, while CJP continued its own campaign against the Election Commission.The two groups had also followed separate courses during the October 10 protests. CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke, TMC chief Mamata Banerjee, AAP leader Arvind Kejriwal and Left leaders were among those detained by Delhi Police. Rahul Gandhi, meanwhile, was in Chennai, though he condemned the police action.Rahul Gandhi made "vote chori" a central political slogan of the opposition. CJP has also adopted it in its street demonstrations. But despite their overlapping demands, the two sides have largely pursued separate protest programmes.This has raised a political question: Why is Congress maintaining a distance from a movement that shares one of its biggest political demands?CJP's agitation against the Election Commission fits into a larger political battle that Congress has already made central to its opposition strategy.Rahul Gandhi's "vote chori" campaign has targeted alleged electoral irregularities in Karnataka, Haryana, Maharashtra and Bihar.The slogan "Vote Chor, Gaddi Chhod", frequently heard at CJP protests, also draws on the political language popularised by Rahul Gandhi.Former Congress national spokesperson Sanjay Jha, however, rejects the suggestion that the two sides are competing for political space."I don't think the battle is between the CJP and the Congress. All members of civil society, students, political parties, intellectuals, authors, activists, NGOs, everyone who's concerned about Indian democracy, are fighting both independently and collectively," he said.Describing CJP as a successful student movement, Jha credited it with bringing the issue to the forefront after investigations by The Indian Express."To say that there is any competition between the two is BJP propaganda, and we should not fall for that," he said.His argument is that the two groups can pursue the same demands without necessarily working together.However, their separate mobilisation has also brought attention to differences in their political approach and relationships with other opposition parties.The BJP and Election Commission, meanwhile, have rejected allegations of electoral manipulation, with the poll body maintaining that revisions are intended to identify ineligible entries and ensure the accuracy of electoral rolls.ALSO READ: 'Can't beat us, threaten us': Rahul thanks protesters after INDIA bloc march to SC The relationship between Congress and CJP is not simply one of competing claims. Their responses to the NEET-UG controversy in 2026 showed that they could support the same cause while maintaining separate political programmes.CJP emerged as a youth-led citizens' movement amid the controversy over alleged examination irregularities. It demanded accountability, education-system reforms and the resignation of then education minister Dharmendra Pradhan.On July 20, CJP organised a "Chalo Sansad" march from Jantar Mantar towards Parliament. Delhi Police stopped the march, citing violations of prohibitory orders and violence, while CJP alleged that police used excessive force against peaceful demonstrators.The following day, Congress organised a separate protest outside Prime Minister Narendra Modi's residence, led by Rahul Gandhi, Mallikarjun Kharge and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra.The party demanded Pradhan's resignation, a parliamentary discussion on paper leaks and education reforms, and an apology to students over the police action.Congress had been raising concerns over examination irregularities before CJP's march. Rahul Gandhi had met students in Kota and Dehradun, while he and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra visited injured students at Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital after the police action.The two sides supported similar demands but organised their programmes independently.That pattern is now visible again in the demonstrations against Gyanesh Kumar.The differences became more visible after CJP's recent outreach in Assam.Congress spokesperson Reetam Singh alleged that CJP co-convenor Ashutosh Ranka had refused a courtesy meeting with Congress leaders, including Assam Congress president Gaurav Gogoi, despite Congress workers helping secure the release of detained CJP members.Singh claimed Ranka had declined to engage because the outreach was considered an AAP initiative."Aam Aadmi Party is known for piggy riding and hijacking issues of others," Singh alleged, accusing AAP of attempting to associate itself with movements led by others.These are Congress's allegations, and do not independently establish why CJP representatives declined the meeting.CJP co-convenor Saurav Das had also criticised what he described as a "self-declared liberal" ecosystem that believed "saving India" and the "Constitution" was its exclusive responsibility.The reference was politically significant because "Save the Constitution" has been a prominent part of Rahul Gandhi's campaign.Ranka also accused sections of that ecosystem of targeting CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke as the movement gained traction.Neither named Congress directly in the posts cited, but the subsequent exchange with Singh brought differences between the two sides into focus.Singh, however, argued that CJP should not be treated as any party's property."Let us keep it civil and issue centric. The cause is bigger than a political party," he said.The exchange suggested disagreements over political associations and coordination, even as both sides continued to raise similar demands.ALSO READ: 'Disclose EC files, set up audit panel': Key points from INDIA bloc's plea in SC The October 10 protest made the difference in political positioning more visible. Mamata Banerjee publicly backed CJP before the demonstration, saying, “We are fully supporting the Cockroach (Janta) Party and all the young generation and students. And my humble request, please stop these atrocities.”She later joined the protest in Delhi, pasting a band-aid over her mouth before being detained alongside TMC leaders. Kejriwal announced that he would attend with his family, while senior Left leaders backed the agitation and challenged restrictions imposed ahead of the demonstration.Congress had not announced participation in the same manner. But Rahul Gandhi's absence from Jantar Mantar did not mean silence on the police action. He condemned the mass detentions, accusing Delhi Police of “thuggery” and alleging that the government was encouraging violence against women and young protesters. He also announced plans for Congress and INDIA bloc leaders to meet the Chief Justice of India.Congress, therefore, continued to challenge the government while pursuing its own political mobilisation and institutional interventions. The distinction is between supporting a cause and joining a particular protest platform.CJP legal head Ratna Singh said the invitation remained open to all parties.“If the Congress is willing to come forward and join the protests, it is most welcome. Not just the Congress, but other parties too. Everyone should come together,” she said.“This is not the time to look at different groups protesting separately. We must see this as a unit, as a team effort, with people raising their voices against the wrongs happening in this country,” she added.Her appeal raises a question that extends beyond Congress: What does solidarity mean when parties agree on an issue but differ over how a protest should be organised, represented and politically sustained?The tensions around CJP have echoes of the 2011 India Against Corruption movement. The BJP publicly backed Anna Hazare's anti-corruption agitation against the Congress-led UPA government. Congress later accused the BJP and RSS of exploiting the movement to undermine its government.The movement's political afterlife was significant. Arvind Kejriwal, one of its prominent figures, went on to form the Aam Aadmi Party in 2012.The parallel is relevant to the present Congress-CJP friction. Congress spokesperson Reetam Singh has alleged that CJP's Assam outreach was viewed as an AAP initiative, accusing the party of “piggy riding and hijacking issues of others”.The allegation raises a question about whether Congress sees CJP not simply as a citizens' movement, but as a platform whose political associations and future trajectory matter.
Article Summary: CJP emerged as a youth-led citizens' movement amid the controversy over alleged examination irregularities. It demanded, education-system reforms and the resignation of then education minister Dharmendra Pradhan. Despite their common demands, the Congress leader and the Cockroach Janta Party leadership have not shared a stage.

Article Title: 60% of 33 lakh who received SIR notices in Delhi are now verified
Article Text:
Disposal of SIR notices expedited after mid-September

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Over 60% of the 33 lakh voters who got SIR notices in Delhi have been verified after the Election Commission eased the verification process late last month.BLOs are now visiting homes to collect documents, instead of requiring people to appear for hearings at govt offices. Also, BLO have been empowered to make corrections for minor issues, such as spelling mistakes, without seeking extensive documentation.About 33 lakh voters, including chief minister Rekha Gupta, AAP national convener Arvind Kejriwal, external affairs minister S Jaishankar and BJP veteran LK Advani got notices in Sept.While over 19 lakh voters were flagged for "logical discrepancies", including mismatches in names and age-related inconsistencies, nearly 14 lakh were classified as "unmapped" because their records could not be linked to the 2002 SIR. The notices sought clarification and supporting documents to verify eligibility for inclusion in the final SIR roll, scheduled for Dec 4.The office of the chief electoral officer of Delhi, in a post on X Monday, said: "We had started a proactive campaign to resolve these issues (discrepancies). By now around 20 lakh cases out of 33 lakh have been resolved. If any person has any grievance, please feel free to contact any of the 14,947 BLOs, 902 AEROs, 70 EROs, 13 DEOs or the CEO.No eligible voter will be excluded from the voter list."An official told TOI, "The disposal of SIR notices was very slow until the third week of Sept but picked up after we introduced new measures. Nearly 15,000 BLOs have been asked to clear at least 10 notices daily. In cases involving logical discrepancies, they have been instructed to verify the voter's age, Indian citizenship and ordinary residence in the constituency. Eligible voters will not be removed merely because of logical inconsistencies in their records. "A few BLOs told TOI they are using BLO declarations to verify voters with minor discrepancies, such as a missing letter in the name, after checking documents and getting the voter's signature on the declarations. Some BLOs said they had been using such declarations for quite some time now.AEROs, meanwhile, have been asked to upload details of resolved cases without delay. "We found that some AEROs were not uploading the cases they had already verified, partly because the deadline for completing the exercise was still weeks away. They have been instructed to ensure that resolved cases are uploaded promptly," said the official.In cases where voters could not be mapped to the previous electoral rolls, BLOs have been asked to clear the cases promptly after taking and checking prescribed documents, such as a voter's date of birth and other documents.Delhi's electoral roll listed 1.56 crore voters in January 2025, days before the assembly elections. In June, when the SIR began, this number had shrunk to 1.45 crore. The draft electoral roll published on Aug 31 had 97.5 lakh voters, with around 47.6 lakh names deleted.EC said a majority of these people had shifted homes and failed to submit enumeration forms. Those who have received SIR notices are among the 97.5 lakh voters. The disposal of SIR notices and completion of verification will continue until Nov 30.
Article Summary: Over 60% of the 33 lakh voters who got SIR notices in Delhi have been verified. The Election Commission eased the verification process late last month. BLOs are now visiting homes to collect documents, instead of requiring people to appear for hearings at govt offices.

Article Title: Jantar Mantar out as protest hub; 3 new venues named
Article Text:
Shifting protests to Burari will reduce chances of traffic congestion: Police

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: For decades, Jantar Mantar offered protesters a place within earshot of Parliament and the seat of govt they sought to hold accountable. Now they will have to make themselves heard from further away.Ramlila Maidan in central Delhi, Burari ground in the north and CBD ground in Shahdara have been designated as the city's new protest sites, replacing Jantar Mantar Road. An order issued by police commissioner Anurag Kumar on Oct 11 said the decision followed recommendations by a ministry of home affairs committee set up to identify suitable venues where citizens could exercise their right to protest.The order said: "On the committee recommendations, Jantar Mantar as a protest venue has been de-notified".While the protest site is called Jantar Mantar, the protests never took place inside the 18th-century, ASI-protected astronomical observatory. They were held on the adjoining Jantar Mantar Road, the starting point of many historic movements.On the face of it, the road is hardly an ideal protest venue. Hemmed in by bungalows and shops, it offers limited space. But crowds find room, spilling into lanes and roads, as was seen during June-July CJP protests and the 2011 India Against Corruption movement.But its location more than makes up for the lack of space. Around 3km from Parliament and barely a kilometre from Connaught Place, it sits amid key govt buildings. It also offers the practical comforts a protest site needs: water, inexpensive food, toilets and tree shade. But its biggest advantage, however, may be that it comes free.The alternatives come with a price. Booking Ramlila Maidan for functions costs Rs 66,080, while Burari and CBD grounds cost approximately Rs 90,000 each (without security deposit). No separate booking category for protests has been introduced yet.Jantar Mantar’s denotification as a protest site came after Supreme Court, on Oct 9, asked authorities to designate a suitable alternative venue for protests. During the hearing, the CJI-led bench said, “The govt and parties are agreeable to the suggestion that it is high time to identify and designate a proper protest site, instead of Jantar Mantar, with basic amenities like water, toilets and healthcare facilities. The competent authorities would consider the suggestion and take an appropriate decision in this regard.”An officer said at Jantar Mantar, a crowd beyond 1,000 leads to crowding and traffic congestion on approach roads. Another officer said the presence of sensitive installations in the vicinity was also a security concern.“If someone disguises themselves as a protester and then moves towards a sensitive installation, it could pose a security threat,” the officer said.Ramlila Maidan can accommodate a crowd of up to 50,000, while Burari ground, which is the largest of the three sites, can hold more than 50,000 people. CBD Ground in Shahdara is across 12 acres.A senior police officer said Ramlila Maidan can host protests and large gatherings. Organisers must apply 10-12 days in advance, after which police coordinate with them on turnout, venue requirements, timings, VIP attendance and the agenda. In 2011, the Anna Hazare-led India Against Corruption movement, which later gave rise to AAP, shifted from Jantar Mantar to Ramlila Maidan as crowds swelled.The proposed shift from Jantar Mantar also raises questions about managing exceptionally large gatherings. One of the organisers of Ramlila events claimed that the turnout at some programmes could exceed 50,000, potentially putting pressure on the arrangements at the designated venues.Police sources said the area of the site at Shahdara will be finalised before infrastructure is set up. With malls, banquet halls and other commercial facilities nearby, clearly demarcating the venue and managing traffic will be key, they said. Once the site is finalised, police infrastructure, including a police post, would be made, the sources added.Burari Ground is an open space. Police sources said the likelihood of such gatherings significantly affecting traffic was relatively low here.
Article Summary: Ramlila Maidan in central Delhi, Burari ground in the north and CBD ground in Shahdara have been designated as the city's new protest sites. Shifting protests to Burari will reduce chances of traffic congestion: Police.

Article Title: CJI: Don't drag SC into political battlefields or bring politics to court
Article Text:
CJI rejects INDIA bloc leaders’ request for meeting over ‘vote chori’

Wherever identified locations are there, protests can be held: SC

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: A day after CJI Surya Kant turned down Congress leadership's request to meet them privately on their "vote chori" charge, saying doing so will violate the principle of separation of powers, SC Monday reiterated that it should not be dragged into political battlefields nor politics be brought into the court."We are not concerned with political parties or their activities. But courts should not be dragged into such kinds of things," said a bench of CJI Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana.In an email response, through which he turned down the request from leaders of opposition in the two Houses of Parliament, Rahul Gandhi and Mallikarjun Kharge, for a face-to-face meeting, CJI had pointed out to them that it was duty-bound to hear petitions against CEC Gyanesh Kumar and those challenging SIR, and indicated that the court will hear those on priority.The CJI-led bench Monday emphasised the need for it to exercise restraint and not enter the political thicket while hearing the complaint that protests and barricades were obstructing lawyers from working.At the commencement of proceedings, senior advocate Atmaram Nadkarni sought urgent hearing on a writ petition filed by a lawyer, saying he could not represent his client at an international arbitration because of protests and preventive measures.Nadkarni was joined by SCBA president Pradeep Rai who said the right to protest must co-exist with the right of other citizens to move and function without hindrance. SC agreed to list both the petitions for hearing on Tuesday along with pleas by Shailendra Mani Tripathi, opposition MPs M A Baby, Manoj Jha and Menaka Guruswamy, who have accused police of using excessive force to quell protests.Rai said, “Institution is performing its institutional duty and we are doing our professional duties. Political parties must not interfere with our domain.”CJI Surya Kant, while saying that court would not wade into others’ turf, said, “Democratic institutions should be allowed to function peacefully and there should not be any impediment in the functioning or movement of lawyers, court staff and litigants.”Following Nadkarni and Rai, advocate G Sankaranarayanan mentioned another petition repeating what was argued — detention of senior advocate Shadan Farasat in an “unseemly” manner — before SC on Sunday and suggested that asking protesters to exercise restraint, be peaceful and cooperate when police was using excessive force, was not fair.“I know SC has repeatedly said we must try to cooperate and exercise restraint. For once I would hope that court would say the same thing to police. That has not come from this bench so far. I am hoping that happens because of excesses they are allowing... the hooligans were roaming around with sticks,” he said.“They have hit children on the head and put out videos and proudly posted the videos saying they have done this and police have done nothing. And we are being told to exercise restraint. I do not know what we have done to be told to exercise restraint. At some point the bench will come to the rescue of the bar and the citizens of this country and send a strong message to the police,” he added.CJI agreed to list the petition on Tuesday but stressed yet again: “I will not allow SC or SC campus to become a political battlefield. We do not want advocates and lawyers to be part of the political battles inside the court premises. Wherever identified locations (for protest) are there, the protests can be held there.”
Article Summary: CJI Surya Kant turned down the request from leaders of opposition in the two Houses of Parliament, Rahul Gandhi and Mallikarjun Kharge, for a face-to-face meeting. CJI pointed out to them that it was duty-bound to hear petitions against CEC Gyanesh Kumar and those challenging SIR.

Article Title: Tyeb Mehta's 'Rickshaw Puller' fetches record 69 crore
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

In 2002, a Tyeb Mehta triptych aptly titled Celebration, from The Times of India collection, set off quite a party in the Indian art market when it became the first Indian painting to cross the crore mark at auction. Though it came in the winter of his life, it was a remarkable milestone for an artist who had spent much of his life in a cramped one-room Bombay apartment that doubled as a studio by day and a bedroom at night. Since that landmark sale, prices for Mehta's paintings, including those featuring his signature bulls, have bull-dozed many old records. The latest is Rickshaw Puller, which fetched Rs 69.1 crore at Volte Una's inaugural auction, setting a world auction record for the artist. The sale surpassed Mehta's earlier personal high of Rs 61.8 crore, set by Trussed Bull in April 2025. Rickshaw Puller is now the fourth-most expensive Indian work of art ever sold at auction. The top spot belongs to Raja Ravi Varma (Rs 167 crore), followed by M F Husain in both second and third.Mehta first encountered rickshaw pullers as a young boy during summer holidays spent with his grandmother in Kolkata and they became a recurring theme.In his early works, the rickshaw puller was a sombre figure rendered in greys and deep reds. In the 2002 painting that set the record on Sunday, man and machine seem almost fused into one, yet one can feel the physical exhaustion of hauling passengers through the city's sweltering streets.The record is particularly striking for an artist known for his exacting standards, who routinely destroyed works he considered unworthy. It also marks a significant debut for Volte Una, a new auction house built around an unusual premise: offering one major work at a time rather than multiple lots in a single sale. The format is designed to give collectors time to engage closely with each artwork before bidding, with an emphasis on privacy."Why should a masterpiece be lost in a crowd? This way, we could expose Tyeb Mehta's painting to the most serious and discreet collectors globally in private settings," said Tushar Jiwarajka, founder of Volte Una. "We have introduced a business model that allows traditional buyer's premium to be significantly reduced, cutting transaction costs for both buyers and sellers."
Article Summary: Rickshaw Puller fetches Rs 69.1 crore at Volte Una's inaugural auction. It is now the fourth-most expensive Indian work of art ever sold at auction. The top spot belongs to Raja Ravi Varma, followed by M F Husain.

Article Title: Uniform themes for sermons across mosques in J&K planned
Article Text:

SRINAGAR: J&K Waqf Board has decided to constitute a core committee comprising imams and religious scholars to finalize common themes for sermons across mosques and shrines on Fridays and other religious occasions.Board chairperson Dr Syed Darakhshan Andrabi told TOI that the decision was taken at a meeting on Saturday following suggestions from imams and Islamic scholars. Around 1,500 muftis, imams, and Islamic scholars attended the meeting.Andrabi added that govt officials have no role in the decision. “The committee will be solely responsible for identifying the issue regarding the uniform sermon,” she said, adding that the move is necessary to deal with issues in the UT, especially social evils, including drug abuse.“There are several sects in J&K and people are associated with different schools of thought. We have no issue with anyone’s sectarian affiliation, and we do not intend to interfere in it. But we don’t want to divide society based on sects,” she added.“I believe a mosque should be a centre for learning and religious knowledge, and this step will help with that a great deal,” she said.
Article Summary: J&K Waqf Board has decided to constitute a core committee comprising imams and religious scholars to finalize common themes for sermons. Board chairperson Dr Syed Darakhshan Andrabi told TOI that the decision was taken at a meeting on Saturday.

Article Title: 'Cannot beat us, threaten us, frighten us': Rahul Gandhi thanks protesters after INDIA bloc march to SC
Article Text:
Rahul thanked his supporters saying, "proud of everybody"

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: RAhul Gandhi on Monday evening thanked his supporters for joining the INDIA bloc march to SC and took jabs at the govenrment and RSS.In a video message posted on X, "I’d like to thank every single person who came out today for this protest. I'd also like to thank the millions of people who showed support in their own way at 3pm. Thank you to the leaders of INDIA bloc, all the workers of the Congress party and workers of the INDIA bloc.Today was a very important day because we needed to show the government that the people of India are not going to be intimidated. You cannot beat us, threaten us, frighten us. We will not accept being bullied," he said.Further taking a jab at RSS, he said, "I was wondering where the cowards of the RSS who were beating the young children day before yesterday were. Where were those people? Because I didn’t see them. When we are standing there and when the people of India are standing there, why don’t you come out? Why don’t you wear your little scarves and come out and see what happens?Because you’re essentially, like the Prime Minister of India, bullies. You cannot stand up. You can only use power to fight."Then, extending his gratitude to the protesters, he added, "It’s very heartening to see what happened.I’m proud of everybody. Everybody worked like a team. As I said in my press conference, there are no parallel protests. It’s one protest, and it’s a protest where everybody is standing together. Every single person is going to stand against these killers of our Constitution, these killers of our democracy. And we’re not going to back down. I’d also like to thank everybody from civil society organisations who came, supported us. We value your support, and we love all of you. Thank you all for coming out and defending the idea of India, the idea of the Constitution, the idea of our democracy."Rahul Gandhi-led INDIA bloc leaders on Monday marched towards the Supreme Court to protest alleged electoral irregularities and theElection Commission ’s Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. The march was halted by police barricades on Bhagwan Das Road in central Delhi, but Rahul Gandhi and 10 other opposition leaders subsequently filed a joint petition in the Supreme Court challenging the EC’s decisions.The plea sought disclosure of the poll panel’s files and safeguards against voter deletions without prior notice and an opportunity to be heard. The march came after Chief Justice of India Surya Kant declined the opposition’s request for a meeting, advising them to pursue the legal route instead.
Article Summary: Rahul Gandhi thanked his supporters saying, "proud of everybody" Gandhi-led INDIA bloc leaders on Monday marched towards the Supreme Court to protest alleged electoral irregularities. The march was halted by police barricades on Bhagwan Das Road in central Delhi.

Article Title: Presidential election today? Trump confuses India with Brazil, claims 125 million voted
Article Text:
Trump says "125 million Indians voted in presidential election today."

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

US President Donald Trump on Monday confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian “presidential election”, while also questioning the integrity of the American voting system.In a post on Truth Social, Trump wrote, “125 Million People voted today in the first round of India’s Presidential Election. The results came out shortly after the vote closed, on the same day!”He then compared the alleged election results with the US electoral process, writing, “In Detroit, Philadelphia, California, and numerous other US Cities and States, the results, with much smaller numbers, will often take weeks to Rig, I mean, calculate. Voting in America is corrupt!!!”However, India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college and not through a direct nationwide popular vote.Trump's remarks came after Brazil held the first round of its presidential election on Sunday, with incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and right-wing challenger Flávio Bolsonaro advancing to the October 25 runoff.With 99.99% of the votes counted, Bolsonaro secured 47.03% of the valid votes, while Lula received 45.16%, according to Brazil's Superior Electoral Court.The figure of around 125 million mentioned by Trump is close to Brazil's total valid votes, which stood at about 125.27 million, suggesting he may have confused the Brazilian election with India.Neither Bolsonaro nor Lula crossed the 50% threshold required to win in the first round, triggering the October 25 runoff, BBC reported.Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of former Brazilian president Jair Bolsonaro, outperformed expectations in the first round and finished ahead of Lula. His strong showing has raised the prospect of a shift to the right in Latin America's largest economy.Brazil has used electronic voting for decades, and electoral authorities said the first-round voting process proceeded smoothly.The Organization of American States' electoral observation mission said “the voting has been going smoothly and under adequate safety conditions.”The rapid announcement of results has also been cited as a strength of Brazil's electronic voting system.“When results take a lot of time, it creates an opening for people to cast doubt on the results, to say there’s been a problem,” Josemar Lauriano Pereira, a 46-year-old lawyer in Rio de Janeiro, told the Associated Press.Trump's post drew reactions on social media, with users pointing out that India does not elect its president through a direct popular vote.One user posted, “Trump living in a different world? Is a presidential election taking place in India? President Donald Trump made the incorrect claim that 125 million people voted in India's "presidential election" today.”Another said, “What is my blud Donald Trump smoking? Why is he mentioning India instead of Brazil when talking about the election?”
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian "presidential election" He also questioned the integrity of the American voting system. India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college.

Article Title: SIR strikes at heart of Constitution: Supreme Court judge Ujjal Bhuyan
Article Text:
File photo: Supreme Court of India Judge Justice Ujjal Bhuyan (PTI Photo)

-

Detaching right to vote from citizen is like taking soul out of body: Bhuyan

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Launching a scathing attack on special intensive revision (SIR) that has resulted in large-scale deletion of names from voter lists across states, Supreme Court judge Justice Ujjal Bhuyan on Sunday said any process disenfranchising millions of Indian citizens was intrinsically arbitrary as it struck at the heart of the Constitution.Discounting the reasons given by govt and EC to justify SIR, which was upheld in the case of the revision of rolls in West Bengal by SC with modifications, Justice Bhuyan said, "No amount of whataboutery can justify it. It strikes at the very heart of Constitution. I would go to the extent of saying that it is a negation of the constitutional order which we have adopted under the Constitution."He was speaking at the moot court valedictory function at Nalsar, Hyderabad.Nalsar students, who had opposed CJI Surya Kant's participation in the convocation ceremony recently, came in for praise from Justice Bhuyan.Also read| Democracy in peril as voters illegally ousted: Former SC judge Justice Rohinton Fali Nariman "One last word about the brilliant students of Nalsar. You have shown to the country and to the world what a university student, that too a student of law, should be. You are brilliant, you are bold, and you are brave," he said.Justice Bhuyan said a citizen’s right to vote was central to the holding of free and fair elections.“Except in the case of a dead voter, the name of a voter once enlisted in the electoral roll cannot be deleted without notice and hearing,” he added.The SC judge said the right to vote or be included in the voters’ list could not be detached from the persona of an Indian citizen.Also read: EC orders special drive to add genuine electors 'left out' during SIR “If it is done, it will be like taking out the soul from the body,” he added. Justice Bhuyan said the Indian Constitution does not provide for two classes of citizens: citizens with voting rights and citizens without voting rights. “Any process which leads to wholesale disenfranchisement of Indian citizens, making them citizens without voting rights, would be violative of Articles 326 and 14 of Constitution of India,” he said.“If any process results in disenfranchising millions and millions of Indian citizens, making them second class citizens in their own country in the sense of being citizens without voting rights, such a process is intrinsically arbitrary,” he added, his remarks coinciding with attacks on EC and govt over SIR by the opposition and others.Justice Bhuyan said the right to vote was intertwined with India’s years of struggle against foreign rule. “It is a manifestation of our freedom achieved after so much struggle and sacrifice. Article 326 (universal adult franchise) cannot be tinkered with at all. No authority can do it, no court can condone it. No one is above Constitution,” he said.
Article Summary: Supreme Court judge Justice Ujjal Bhuyan said any process disenfranchising millions of Indian citizens was intrinsically arbitrary as it struck at the heart of the Constitution. He was speaking at the moot court valedictory function at Nalsar, Hyderabad. “If it is done, it will be like taking out the soul from the body,” he added.

Article Title: Why are Tom Brady and Bill Belichick facing backlash? New England Patriots legends miss 25th-anniversary Super Bowl reunion as Giants appearance raises questions
Article Text:
Why are Tom Brady and Bill Belichick facing backlash? New England Patriots legends miss 25th-anniversary Super Bowl reunion as Giants appearance raises questions(Getty)

Why Tom Brady and Bill Belichick are facing criticism over the Patriots reunion

Bill Belichick's Giants reunion adds another layer to the debate

Tom Brady and Bill Belichick helped build the New England Patriots into an NFL dynasty. However, their absence from the team's 25th-anniversary celebration of its first Super Bowl title has drawn criticism. The backlash grew after Belichick attended a reunion with the New York Giants just eight days earlier. For Patriots fans, the issue is not just about two legends missing an event. It is also about the small gesture they could have made to honor the team that changed NFL history.The Patriots celebrated their Super Bowl XXXVI championship on Oct. 11, 2026, before facing the Las Vegas Raiders at Gillette Stadium. Former players returned for the occasion, but Brady and Belichick did not attend or send video messages. Their absence became a talking point on Boston sports radio, where hosts questioned why the two central figures could not spare a few seconds to acknowledge their former teammates.The criticism gained momentum on 98.5 The Sports Hub after hosts Michael Felger, Tony Massarotti and Jim Murray discussed the missing Patriots legends. Murray argued that a short phone-recorded message would have been enough to recognize the anniversary."All it takes is two seconds. Just turn that phone around, film a video, send it off to someone at the Patriots," Murray said on the show, as the hosts discussed the October 11 celebration.The point was simple. Neither man needed to attend the ceremony in person to acknowledge the achievement. A brief greeting could have recognized the players who helped New England win its first Super Bowl and begin one of the NFL's greatest dynasties.Brady led the Patriots to a 20-17 victory over the St. Louis Rams in Super Bowl XXXVI on February 3, 2002. The win marked his first Super Bowl title and Belichick's first as New England's head coach. It also began a partnership that produced six championships together.That history made their absence especially noticeable. The celebration also honored kicker Adam Vinatieri, whose 48-yard field goal sealed the Super Bowl victory as time expired.Belichick's recent appearance at a New York Giants reunion gave the discussion an extra edge. On October 3, 2026, he attended a dinner marking the 40th anniversary of the Giants' first Super Bowl championship, won during the 1986 season.Belichick served as the Giants' defensive coordinator from 1985 to 1990 and played a key role in their championship success. He attended the dinner after North Carolina, where he now coaches, lost to Notre Dame.The contrast prompted questions about why he could make time for the Giants but not take part in the Patriots' celebration eight days later. Still, neither Belichick nor Brady publicly explained their absence in the material surrounding the event, so their reasons remain unclear.Their past comments about each other also show that their relationship cannot be reduced to a rivalry over credit. On his podcast in 2023, Brady rejected the familiar debate over who deserved more recognition for New England's success."From my standpoint, I think it's always such a stupid conversation to say, 'Brady vs. Belichick' because, in my mind, that's not what a partnership is about," Brady said during the podcast discussion.Belichick also praised their working relationship during Brady's retirement podcast, recalling their football conversations and the respect they shared.Meanwhile, New England's anniversary ceremony went ahead on October 11. Joe Andruzzi carried two American flags onto the field, recalling his gesture after the September 11 attacks, while Vinatieri received his Pro Football Hall of Fame Ring of Excellence at halftime.The Patriots lost 45-17 to the Raiders that day, but the celebration still honored the team that started their championship era. Brady and Belichick's absence, however, became another talking point surrounding a historic reunion.
Article Summary: New England Patriots legends Tom Brady and Bill Belichick missed team's 25th- anniversary celebration of its first Super Bowl title. Their absence became a talking point on Boston sports radio, where hosts questioned why the two central figures could not spare a few seconds to acknowledge their former teammates. Belichick attended a reunion with the New York Giants just eight days earlier.

Article Text:

MUMBAI: Tushar Deshpande, eager to make a point after being left out of the India A squad for the upcoming New Zealand tour, produced a fiery spell on his 50th first-class appearance to put Mumbai in complete control against Chandigarh at the Wankhede Stadium on Monday.Deshpande took 5/17 in seven overs, including a hat-trick, as Chandigarh were bowled out for 78 in 19.1 overs in reply to Mumbai’s 429 on day two of their Ranji Trophy Elite Group D match. Mumbai enforced the follow on, and Deshpande struck again in the only over of Chandigarh’s second innings, cleaning up Vishu Kashyap with another sharp incoming delivery. Chandigarh ended the day at 0/1, with Deshpande’s match figures reading 6/17. With national selector SS Das watching from the MCA President’s Box, Deshpande delivered a statement performance, appearing a threat with almost every ball.Mohit Avasthi also joined the act, taking 3/9 in six overs, as Mumbai secured a massive 351-run first-innings lead. On Tuesday, the hosts will look to wrap up a bonus-point win. Chandigarh, who entered domestic cricket only in 2018-19, collapsed to their lowest first-class total.Deshpande began by having opener Arsalan Khan chop one onto his stumps in the seventh over. He then entered the record books in the 11th over, dismissing Arjun Azad, Shivam Bhambri and Deepinder Kush off successive deliveries.Azad top-edged a hook to Sylvester D’Souza at long leg, Bhambri was bowled by a pacy delivery that hit the top of off stump, and Kush edged to Yashasvi Jaiswal at first slip.Deshpande became the sixth Mumbai bowler to take a first-class hat-trick, and the first to achieve the feat at the Wankhede. Jahangir Khot, Umesh Kulkarni, Abdul Ismail, Royston Dias and Shardul Thakur are the other Mumbai bowlers with firstclass hat-tricks. It took Deshpande just 20 balls to complete his sixth firstclass five-wicket haul, trapping Raj Angad Bawa lbw for a four-ball duck. Chandigarh lost five wickets for four runs, sliding from 25/1 to 29/6.Earlier in the day, Deshpande had also chipped in with 44 off 47 balls, hitting four fours and two sixes. Chandigarh may have been dismissed for less than 50 but scored 51 off 6.1 overs from Mumbai’s third seamer Sylvester D’Souza, who took two wickets. Mumbai vice-captain Ayush Mhatre did not take the field, with Suved Parkar substituting for him. Earlier, Mumbai’s lower order again made a significant contribution. Resuming on 249/5, Mumbai lost captain Siddhesh Lad for 86 and Shams Mulani for 39 early in the day, but Tanush Kotian , Avasthi and Deshpande lifted the total to 429.Kotian made 58 off 91 balls, while Avasthi scored an unbeaten 56 off 119 balls, his fourth first-class half-century. The trio helped Mumbai add 180 runs on Monday and kept Chandigarh in the field for two sessions.
Article Summary: Tushar Deshpande takes hat-trick on 50th first-class appearance for Mumbai. Chandigarh bowled out for 78 in reply to Mumbai’s 429 on day two of their Ranji Trophy Elite Group D match.

Article Title: Travis Kelce's mom Donna Kelce joined global giving campaign at Kansas City's Union Station
Article Text:
Travis Kelce and Donna Kelce (Image via Getty)

Donna Kelce and Tammy Reid support the Giving Machine campaign

Kansas City Giving Machines benefit seven local charities

Donna Kelce has become a familiar face to football fans, but her time in Kansas City has also highlighted a cause beyond the NFL. In November 2023, the mother of Travis Kelce and Jason Kelce joined forces with Tammy Reid, wife of Kansas City Chiefs head coach Andy Reid, for a charitable initiative designed to make giving easier. The campaign brought a different kind of excitement to Union Station, inviting visitors to support people in need through a simple act of generosity. It also connected the city's holiday spirit with charities working to improve lives locally and around the world.Donna Kelce stayed in Kansas City after watching the Chiefs face the Philadelphia Eagles on Monday night. Although the game brought her sons' football careers into focus, the following day's plans shifted attention towards community service.On November 21, 2023, Donna and Tammy Reid were scheduled to help launch the annual Light the World campaign at Union Station. The initiative used special vending machines to turn charitable donations into practical support for people facing different challenges.Unlike traditional vending machines, the Giving Machines do not dispense products for buyers to take home. Instead, visitors choose an item or service to donate towards, with options that include meals, school supplies, shoes for children, eye exams and toys.The concept offers a direct and accessible way for people to contribute during the holiday season. Rather than simply making a general donation, participants can select the type of assistance they want to provide.Travis Kelce also appeared in promotional messages for the campaign. He playfully described the Giving Machine as “a big red box,” helping introduce the initiative to a wider audience. Actor Eric Stonestreet was among the other celebrities featured in promotional material.The campaign had a strong local focus, with donations supporting seven organisations serving people across the Kansas City area. These included Foster Adopt Connect, Kansas City Hospice & Palliative Care, reStart, Ronald McDonald House Charities of Kansas City, the Mayor’s Christmas Tree Fund, Science City and Westside Community Action Network.Each organisation serves a different need, from supporting children and families to providing hospice care, housing assistance and educational opportunities. The campaign gave visitors an opportunity to direct their generosity towards causes that mattered to them.The Giving Machines were installed at two locations inside Union Station: Level One in the Grand Hall and Level B near the Regnier Extreme Screen.Kansas City was among 61 cities worldwide hosting the machines in 2023, marking their third year in the city.For Donna Kelce and Tammy Reid, the campaign offered a chance to use their public profiles to draw attention to community needs. It also gave Kansas City residents and visitors a practical way to make charitable giving part of their Thanksgiving and Christmas traditions.
Article Summary: Donna Kelce and Tammy Reid support the Giving Machine campaign. Kansas City Giving Machines benefit seven local charities. The initiative used special vending machines to turn charitable donations into practical support for people facing different challenges. Unlike traditional vending machines, the Giving Machines do not dispense products for buyers to take home.

Article Title: "I'm just trying to do the best": Naomi Osaka reveals how daughter Shai helped her see life beyond tennis after mental health struggles
Article Text:
Naomi Osaka credits motherhood for changing her mindset

Naomi Osaka's 2021 French Open withdrawal brought mental health into focus

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Naomi Osaka has found a new sense of balance in life, and tennis is no longer the only thing that defines her happiness. The four-time Grand Slam champion has spoken candidly about her mental health journey, revealing how becoming a mother has helped her see the sport differently. With her daughter, Shai, playing a central role in her life, Osaka is learning to value the moments she spends on the court without letting results dictate her happiness. Her latest admission offers a glimpse into the personal growth behind her return to competitive tennis.Osaka shared her thoughts after beginning her China Open campaign with a hard-fought victory over Maria Timofeeva. The 12th seed won 6-3, 3-6, 6-3 to reach the next round, but her comments about life beyond tennis drew attention.Asked whether she felt happier despite not adding another Grand Slam title to her record in recent years, Osaka pointed to a change in priorities. Her daughter, Shai, has helped her build an identity that extends beyond her achievements as a professional athlete."I mean, I think it's all about mindset. I feel like I'm definitely happier now. It's because, like, tennis isn't my entire life. I've managed to build a life outside of that.My daughter's a huge part of it. I feel like it's also a part of growing up. I think I was very sheltered as a kid. I literally ate, slept, and breathed for tennis. Now it's just like growing up being grateful to be able to play the sport, but understanding that nothing lasts forever. I'm just trying to do the best with the time that I have," said Naomi Osaka.The Japanese star's comments reflect a shift in how she measures success. Instead of allowing rankings and trophies to shape her entire outlook, she now places greater value on the life she has built away from competition.Her most recent Grand Slam triumph came at the 2021 Australian Open, where she defeated Jennifer Brady in the final. Since then, her journey has included challenges that extended far beyond tennis.Osaka's decision to prioritise her wellbeing became a major talking point during the 2021 French Open. After skipping her first-round post-match press conference, she received a $15,000 fine and faced warnings about possible further penalties.On May 31, she withdrew from the tournament, explaining that she had experienced long periods of depression since her 2018 US Open victory. She also described the anxiety she felt before speaking publicly."This isn't a situation I ever imagined or intended when I posted a few days ago. I think now the best thing for the tournament, the other players and my wellbeing is that I withdraw so that everyone can get back to focusing on the tennis going on in Paris."The truth is I have suffered long bouts of depression since the US Open in 2018 and I have had a really hard time coping with that. Though the tennis press has always been kind to me (and I want to apologise to all the cool journalists who I may have hurt), I am not a natural public speaker and get huge waves of anxiety before I speak to the world's media," wrote Naomi Osaka.She also explained why she had chosen to skip media appearances."I get really nervous and find it stressful to always try to engage and give you the best answers I can. So here in Paris I was already feeling vulnerable and anxious, so I thought it was better to exercise self-care and skip the press conferences. I announced it preemptively because I do feel like the rules are quite outdated in parts and I wanted to highlight that."Osaka later expressed her intention to work with the tour to improve the experience for players, journalists and fans.Her latest reflections show how her priorities have evolved since that difficult period. As she continues her China Open campaign, she will face Sara Bejlek in the round of 32, carrying a perspective shaped by both her career and motherhood.
Article Summary: Naomi Osaka has spoken candidly about her mental health journey. The four-time Grand Slam champion has found a new sense of balance in life. Her daughter, Shai, has helped her build an identity that extends beyond tennis. Osaka's decision to prioritise her wellbeing became a major talking point.

UNICEF India on Sunday named Indian women’s cricket captain Smriti Mandhana as its Celebrity Advocate on the occasion of the International Day of the Girl.Through this role, she will promote equal opportunities for girls and support efforts to improve their health, well-being, education and leadership."I am deeply honoured to join UNICEF India as a Celebrity Advocate. Growing up playing cricket taught me that every dream begins with an opportunity. With hard work, determination, and encouragement, that opportunity can turn into something extraordinary. Every child and young person deserves the chance to dream big and reach their full potential," Mandhana said.Mandhana has previously supported UNICEF-ICC campaigns promoting gender equality and life skills, along with UNICEF’s Promise to Children campaign. Our coaches adapt well, communicate well and work effectively in different cultures.We’re a nation of about five-and-a-half million people, so there’s a saying that we punch above our weight. The momentum shifts, the tactical battles and the nuances of the game are incredibly appealing.We’re very committed to it.Yes. Article Title: 'We are enough for each other': Prithvi Shaw, Akriti Agarwal reunite weeks after calling off engagement
Article Text:
Prithvi Shaw and Akriti Agarwal (Image credit: Instagram)

Engagement called off in September

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Indian cricketer Prithvi Shaw and actor-influencer Akriti Agarwal have decided to give their relationship another chance, weeks after calling off their engagement.Akriti confirmed their reunion through an Instagram statement on Monday, admitting that other people’s opinions had influenced her decision to end the relationship.In a post titled "A personal clarification", Akriti said she had allowed people close to her to influence how she viewed Shaw and their relationship.“When I called off our engagement, I let the opinions of people close to me – who seemed to know our relationship better than we did – influence how I saw my fiancee and our relationship,” she wrote.“I feel I was misguided, and I made a decision without giving us the honest conversation we deserved.”Akriti said the two have since had honest conversations, understood each other better and decided to reunite. She also took responsibility for the hurt caused by her earlier decision and asked people to respect their choice.“Together, we are enough for each other, and we don't need anyone else,” she wrote. Shaw later shared her statement on his Instagram story.Shaw and Akriti announced their engagement in March 2026, sharing pictures of the proposal on social media.However, in September, Akriti revealed that they had decided to part ways, citing different goals and circumstances.Her latest statement confirms that they have reconciled, although neither has publicly explained all the details behind their separation and reunion.Away from his personal life, Shaw is also working to revive his cricket career.The 26-year-old rose to prominence after captaining India to the Under-19 World Cup title in 2018 and scoring a century on his Test debut against the West Indies later that year. However, injuries and inconsistent performances have kept him away from the national team.He moved from Mumbai to Maharashtra ahead of the 2025-26 domestic season in search of a fresh start and scored 222 against Chandigarh in the Ranji Trophy last season.Shaw has begun the 2026-27 domestic season positively, scoring 70 off 73 balls for Maharashtra against Services in New Delhi on Sunday.
Article Summary: Indian cricketer Prithvi Shaw and actor-influencer Akriti Agarwal have reconciled. The couple announced their engagement in March 2026. In September, they announced they had decided to part ways, citing different goals and circumstances.

Article Title: Shubman Gill pips Abhishek Sharma to make history with fifth ICC Player of the Month award as Shafali Verma completes India’s double
Article Text:
Shubman Gill and Shafali Verma (ANI/IANS Photos)

Gill's record fifth award after stunning ODI double

Shafali completes India's double after Asia Cup and Asian Games heroics

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

India achieve the award double for third time

NEW DELHI: Shubman Gill has extended his dominance at the ICC Player of the Month awards, while Shafali Verma has added another individual honour to India's recent run of success, with the two stars named the men's and women's Players of the Month for September.Gill claimed the award for a record fifth time in the men's category after a sensational ODI series against the West Indies, while Shafali earned her second monthly honour following influential performances in India's Women's Asia Cup and Asian Games triumphs. The double marked the third time India have swept both awards in the same month.Gill's latest recognition puts him alongside West Indies captain Hayley Matthews, who has also won the ICC Player of the Month award five times across the men's and women's categories.Gill's September campaign was headlined by two remarkable innings against the West Indies. He began with a commanding 110 in the opening ODI in Thiruvananthapuram, helping India secure an eight-wicket victory and take a 1-0 lead in the series.The India captain raised the bar in the next match, smashing 223 off just 133 deliveries in a breathtaking display of strokeplay. His innings powered India through a successful chase of 406, with the hosts winning by eight wickets with 39 balls to spare.The double-century was the quickest in ODI history, adding another milestone to Gill's growing list of achievements.“It feels fantastic to win my fifth ICC Player of the Month award, and I am grateful to the panel for this honour. It was immensely satisfying to score those runs and even more special to be part of successful run chases in front of our home fans, whose support always gives us an extra boost,” Gill said.The right-hander also highlighted the evolving demands of ODI cricket and India's preparations for the next men's World Cup.“The pace of ODI cricket has gone up significantly, and you must think on your feet, assess the conditions quickly and adapt to the demands of the pitch and the target. With the ICC Men’s Cricket World Cup in southern Africa next year, we are determined to keep raising our standards and build a strong and balanced team capable of rising to the challenges ahead,” he added.Gill's previous monthly awards came in January and September 2023, followed by February and July 2025. His fifth win further extends his record in the men's category.Shafali's September recognition reflects her impact across two major tournaments, where her aggressive batting and useful contributions with the ball helped India enjoy a successful run.The opener finished as India's leading run-scorer during their Women's Asia Cup-winning campaign, accumulating 360 runs at a strike rate of 184.61. She also picked up six wickets during the period, underlining her all-round contribution.She carried that form into the Asian Games, producing an unbeaten 100 against Bangladesh in the semi-final before scoring 48 in the final against Sri Lanka.“It is an incredible honour to win the ICC Player of the Month award again. It was immensely satisfying to play my part in our victories at the Asia Cup and the Asian Games, and winning this award makes those triumphs even more special,” Shafali said.The award is her second, following her first win in November 2025 after a match-winning performance in the Women's World Cup final against South Africa in Navi Mumbai.“I am excited about the months ahead and determined to keep performing at my best, with the ICC Women’s Champions Trophy in February next year, another tournament to look forward to. The memory of winning the World Cup is still so fresh and special, and I can’t wait to be back on the field for an ICC tournament on home soil. It promises to be an unforgettable experience!” she added.India's latest sweep is the fifth occasion in the award's history that players from the same cricket board have won both monthly honours, and the third time India have achieved the feat.Jasprit Bumrah and Smriti Mandhana claimed the men's and women's awards in June 2024, while Abhishek Sharma and Mandhana completed the double in September 2025.The September men's shortlist also featured India opener Abhishek Sharma and Zimbabwe captain Sikandar Raza. Sri Lanka captain Chamari Athapaththu and India left-arm spinner Sree Charani were nominated in the women's category.
Article Summary: Gill claims record fifth award after stunning ODI double against West Indies. Verma completes India's double after Asia Cup and Asian Games heroics. The double marked the third time India have swept both awards in the same month. Abhisk Sharma and Mandhana completed the September men's shortlist.

Article Title: UK's concrete 'sound mirrors' were built after World War 1 to catch bombers; they were abandoned in 1939 because...
Article Text:
The Denge Sound Mirrors near Greatstone Lakes in Kent, built between 1928 and 1930 to detect enemy aircraft by sound.

Britain built sound mirrors because World War 1 left its coast exposed

Radar arrived before the sound mirrors could be perfected

Long before radar screens tracked enemy planes, Britain tried to hear them coming. Three giant concrete structures on the Kent coast, known as the Denge Sound Mirrors, were built between 1928 and 1930 to pick up the drone of approaching aircraft and give the country a few extra minutes of warning. By 1939, they had been abandoned, made obsolete by the arrival of radar.The mirrors still stand near Greatstone Lakes, inside an RSPB nature reserve at Dungeness. From a distance they look like carved stone, but they are made of concrete. Today they draw walkers, photographers and history buffs, and they offer a rare look at how Britain built its early warning systems between the two world wars.The project was led by Dr William Sansome Tucker, a physicist who specialised in acoustics. Britain's coastal towns had suffered heavily from air raids during World War 1, and the government was keen to avoid a repeat. It put serious money into acoustic research that could warn of incoming bombers, and the Denge mirrors were one of the results.Each mirror has a different shape and faces a slightly different direction. Their curved surfaces reflected the sound of aircraft engines onto a focal point, amplifying it enough for operators to pick it up.Depending on which mirror caught the noise, technicians could tell where a threat was coming from and when to scramble fighters.The mirrors had a maximum detection range of about 20 miles. That sounds short today, but aircraft of the late 1920s were slow enough that 20 miles gave defenders time to respond.The first mirror, a 20-foot dish completed in 1928, did not work as intended. Engineers kept refining the design, adding a 30-foot dish and then, in 1930, a 200-foot curved wall that covered a much wider arc of sky. The pace of that iteration was quick for its time.It was not quick enough. Aircraft were getting faster every year, which shrank the warning window, and the mirrors struggled to separate engine noise from wind and other background sounds. When radio-based detection arrived in the late 1930s, it could spot planes far beyond 20 miles, in any weather. The sound mirrors were left to the marshes.They are not the only wartime oddity still standing in England's south. Near Shoreham Airport in Sussex, a graffiti-covered concrete dome once trained anti-aircraft gunners by projecting films of enemy planes onto its ceiling. It was one of 43 such domes built in 1943, and only six survive. The Denge mirrors belong to an earlier chapter of the same story: a country learning, one experiment at a time, how to see what was coming.
Article Summary: Britain built sound mirrors because World War 1 left its coast exposed. The Denge Sound Mirrors were built between 1928 and 1930 to pick up the drone of approaching aircraft and give the country a few extra minutes of warning. By 1939, they had been abandoned, made obsolete by the arrival of radar.

Steve Smith

Former Australia captain Steve Smith has been cleared of concussion and resumed fielding duties on the fifth day of the first Test against South Africa at Kingsmead in Durban on Tuesday, after undergoing a series of clinical assessments following a blow to the helmet.The 37-year-old batter was struck by a short-pitched delivery from Anrich Nortje during Australia's second innings. Smith attempted to duck under the ball but misjudged its trajectory as it failed to rise as much as he expected.Although he continued batting after the incident, scoring 27 off 41 balls before being caught at long-on off Simon Harmer, Smith did not take the field when South Africa began their second innings on Monday. Michael Neser served as his substitute fielder during that session.However, Smith returned to the field on Tuesday morning after being cleared under Cricket Australia's concussion protocols. He was stationed in the slip cordon when South Africa resumed their chase and subsequently took a catch to dismiss Kyle Verreynne off Matt Renshaw's bowling."Steve Smith has undergone a series of clinical assessments over the past 24 hours in accordance with Cricket Australia’s concussion protocols and has been cleared to take the field this morning," Cricket Australia said in a statement.The incident brought back memories of Smith's previous concussion scare during the 2019 Ashes in England, when he was struck on the head by fast bowler Jofra Archer and forced to miss part of a Test match.Smith's return to the field came after medical assessments over the preceding 24 hours, with Australia following the prescribed protocols before allowing the experienced batter to resume his duties.His presence was a boost for Australia as they pushed for victory in the series opener, with South Africa mounting a determined resistance on the final day.South Africa resumed at 102/4 on Tuesday, needing another 319 runs to win. They reached 166/6 by lunch after Australia struck twice to strengthen their grip on the contest.Opener Aiden Markram led the home side's resistance, remaining unbeaten on 69 at the interval alongside Marco Jansen on seven. The pair had to rebuild after Wiaan Mulder's patient 69-run fifth-wicket partnership with Markram ended when Josh Hazlewood had Mulder caught behind by Alex Carey.Part-time spinner Matt Renshaw then dismissed Verreynne, who made just one before edging a reckless shot to Smith at slip.Renshaw has been Australia's standout performer with the bat, having scored 190 in the first innings and 82 in the second, before adding two wickets to his match contribution.Australia needed four more wickets at lunch to seal victory in the opening Test. The second Test of the series is scheduled to begin in Gqeberha on Sunday.
Article Summary: Steve Smith cleared of concussion after blow to the helmet. Former Australia captain was struck by short-pitched delivery from Anrich Nortje. Smith took a catch to dismiss Kyle Verreynne off Matt Renshaw's bowling. Australia needed four more wickets at lunch to seal victory in the opening Test.

Article Title: Formula 1 to return to Africa after 37 years as Rwanda signs 10-year deal to host Grand Prix
Article Text:
F1 last raced in Africa at the Kyalami Circuit back in 1993 (Image: F1)

Rwanda to build purpose-built F1 circuit in Bugesera

Stefano Domenicali calls Rwanda deal a landmark moment

Paul Kagame hails historic moment for Africa

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Inaugural race details awaited

Formula 1 is set to make a historic return to Africa for the first time since 1993, with Rwanda securing a 10-year agreement to host a Grand Prix from the early 2030s. The announcement, made by F1 on Tuesday, marks a major step towards fulfilling the championship’s long-standing ambition of bringing the sport back to the continent.The race will be held at a purpose-built circuit in Bugesera, south of Rwanda’s capital, Kigali, once construction is completed. The venue is expected to become a major motorsport and entertainment destination, while the return of F1 will bring the world championship to Africa after more than three decades.The last Formula 1 race on the continent was the South African Grand Prix at Kyalami in 1993. Rwanda’s entry into the calendar would also mean that F1 will race across every inhabited continent.The proposed circuit will be located approximately 40 kilometres south of Kigali, adjacent to the new Kigali International Airport. Construction is expected to be completed in the early 2030s.Beyond hosting Formula 1 race weekends, the facility is planned as a year-round destination for motorsport events, major gatherings, conferences and entertainment. According to F1, the project is intended to support long-term economic growth and investment across Rwanda and the wider region.Formula 1 president and CEO Stefano Domenicali described the agreement as a landmark moment, emphasising the sport’s commitment to returning to Africa through a long-term partnership."Today is a landmark moment for Formula 1. With Rwanda joining the calendar from the next decade, our sport will race in every inhabited continent, bringing the World Championship closer than ever to fans around the globe," Domenicali said.He added that Africa had always been part of Formula 1’s future and that the championship wanted to return with the right partner, a long-term commitment and a clear vision for creating a meaningful impact. Domenicali thanked Rwanda President Paul Kagame, the Rwandan government, the Rwanda Development Board, FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem and others involved in securing the agreement.Rwanda President Paul Kagame welcomed the agreement, describing it as a significant moment for the continent after more than three decades without a Formula 1 race."Today belongs to Africa. For more than three decades, the world’s premier motorsport championship has raced without this continent, and that changes with this agreement," Kagame said.He added that Rwanda was proud to host the Formula 1 African Grand Prix and share the occasion with fans across the continent, particularly young people who could aspire to careers as engineers, technicians, entrepreneurs and drivers."Our aim was never a single race weekend, but a lasting benefit for our people," he said, referring to the planned circuit and its proximity to the new international airport.The Rwandan president thanked Domenicali, Formula 1 and Ben Sulayem for their role in bringing the agreement to fruition, adding that the country looked forward to welcoming the world for the African Grand Prix.While the 10-year agreement establishes the framework for Formula 1’s return to Africa, the exact date of the inaugural Rwandan Grand Prix remains unconfirmed. Further announcements on circuit development milestones, the race schedule and plans for the event are expected in due course.
Article Summary: Formula 1 set to return to Africa for the first time since 1993. Rwanda has signed a 10-year agreement to host a Grand Prix. The race will be held at a purpose-built circuit in Bugesera, south of Rwanda’s capital, Kigali.
