NEW DELHI: Across history, past and present, virtually every urban centre, from Kolkata, Mumbai, and Chennai to smaller towns such as Jaipur and Panaji, has its own protest site.Over the years, authorities have denotified several in the name of public convenience, while others continue to serve as free speech zones or squares of resistance, news agency PTI reported.Some were sites of British oppression, while many acquired cult status because of their association with Mahatma Gandhi, the original satyagrahi.After Delhi Police denotified Jantar Mantar in the heart of the city as a protest site on Monday, attention turned to other “Jantar Mantars” across the country, most of them located close to the seat of power.Here is a look at some of these sites, each evocatively named to recall its place in history.Originally part of a vast open tract of land called the Esplanade, Azad Maidan was a site of public executions during the 1857 uprising.It later became a key venue for nationalist protests during the freedom movement.Mahatma Gandhi held a massive rally here in 1931, PTI reported.A few kilometres away is Mumbai’s other protest site, August Kranti Maidan, from where Gandhi launched the Quit India Movement in 1942.Shivaji Park, another venue for major political gatherings and public rallies, is also nearby.Modelled on London’s Hyde Park, Freedom Park has a dedicated space for public rallies and protests.The site originally housed a central jail built by the British, where many freedom fighters were imprisoned and sent to the gallows.After Independence, several opposition leaders, including Atal Bihari Vajpayee and LK Advani, were imprisoned here during the Emergency, PTI reported.The jail was converted into Freedom Park in 2008, and the site also houses a jail museum.Originally a parade ground for British East India Company forces following their victory in the Battle of Plassey, Brigade Parade Ground became a central protest venue during the freedom movement.This included a rally organised by Deshbandhu Chittaranjan Das against the Rowlatt Act.India’s first prime minister, Jawaharlal Nehru, held a public reception for Soviet leaders here.Indira Gandhi also invited Mujibur Rehman for an event at the ground after the formation of Bangladesh following India’s victory against Pakistan, PTI reported.The ground has also witnessed massive rallies organised by successive state governments, including the Left, the Trinamool Congress and now the BJP.Other protest sites in Kolkata include Rani Rashmoni Avenue near Esplanade, Shaheed Minar Maidan and College Square.Previously known as Patna Lawns and Bankipore Maidan, this sprawling ground near the banks of the Ganga has hosted several historic protests and rallies.The British developed it for military drills, horse racing, polo and a golf course.It later became a key rally site during the freedom movement, including during the Champaran and Quit India movements, PTI reported.Muhammad Ali Jinnah hosted a key Muslim League session here in 1938, while Subhas Chandra Bose held a Forward Bloc meeting in 1939.After Independence, the ground became the launchpad for the JP movement when Jayaprakash Narayan called for ‘Total Revolution’ against the Emergency.Named after Bal Gangadhar Tilak and located on Marina Beach, Tilak Ghat was a key protest site during the freedom struggle.It hosted several prominent leaders, including Mahatma Gandhi, Subhas Chandra Bose and Annie Besant. However, it is no longer a designated protest site.Other protest sites in Chennai include Valluvar Kottam and Swami Sivananda Salai.In March 2025, police designated Swami Sivananda Salai as an alternative venue for protests after stopping permissions for demonstrations at Valluvar Kottam.Long before Jantar Mantar became known as a protest site rather than an observatory, the expansive Boat Club lawns, a few kilometres away near Parliament and Rashtrapati Bhavan, served as the primary venue for rallies, demonstrations and agitations.The 1988 farmers’ agitation led by Mahendra Singh Tikait, who brought a crowd of more than five lakh people along with tractors and cattle, prompted a clampdown on protests at Boat Club.In 1993, protests were banned at the site following the Babri Masjid demolition.A court order in 2018 briefly allowed it to serve as a protest venue again, alongside Jantar Mantar, PTI reported.Not far from these two Lutyens’ Delhi sites, Ramlila Ground remains a designated protest venue, though at a cost.Syama Prasad Mookerjee launched a satyagraha at Ramlila Ground in 1952, demanding the complete integration of Jammu and Kashmir into the Indian Union.Socialist leader Jayaprakash Narayan addressed a massive rally here on June 25, 1975, the day the Emergency was declared. The ground was also the site of the 2011 anti-corruption movement.Other cities too have designated protest sites.Lucknow has Eco Garden, Panaji has Azad Maidan and Campal Parade Ground, Hyderabad has Dharna Chowk, Gun Park and Livery Circle, while Jaipur has Shaheed Smarak.(With agency inputs)
Article Summary: After Delhi Police denotified Jantar Mantar as a protest site on Monday, attention turned to other 'Jantars' across the country. Locations like Azad Maidan in Mumbai and Gandhi Maidan, Patna, Brigade Parade Ground in Kolkata have hosted significant events. Some were sites of British oppression, while many acquired cult status because of their association with Mahatma Gandhi.

Article Title: The rise, fall and nostalgia of Hauz Khas Village
Article Text:
Hauz Khas Village of the late ’90s and early 2000s had this unique blend of affordable and aspirational that made it appealing to youngsters back then





From cosy boutique stores to the highly aspirational multi-designer store, quaint cafes and hidden coffee spots in the lanes, small artisanal shops to art galleries, and vintage stores to hidden thrift stores – Hauz Khas Village of the late ’90s and early 2000s had this unique blend of affordable and aspirational that made it appealing to youngsters back then. If vibe had been the buzzword in the ’90s, Hauz Khas Village definitely had the right one.And all those who made it their adda in the early 2000s would agree. Be it gedi maarna, a picnic in Deer Park, sitting around the lake, checking out stores or club-hopping at night, there was enough to spend an entire day at HKV. For millennials, weekends would often mean heading to HKV, and there was a certain kind of pride worth flaunting if you knew all the new places there or had partied at almost every lounge and club.There was also a time when you didn’t need to check Instagram to know which place was trending. You heard about a new opening from friends, landed there over the weekend and then probably hopped to another place in the same lane. We knew which narrow staircase led to which club, which terrace had a good view and where you were most likely to bump into half the people you knew. And yes, getting a table on a Saturday night without a reservation was almost an achievement.Its massive popularity was also one of the reasons why HKV became a hotspot for clubs and restaurants. There was a phase when almost every week would mean a new opening. The narrow lanes got more crowded, parking became a nightmare and restaurants and clubs mushroomed in buildings that were clearly not meant to handle that kind of footfall, raising concerns over fire safety and other issues. But despite everything, millennials didn’t switch loyalties from their favourite hangout spot for a long time. We complained about the traffic, parking and crowds, and still landed there the next weekend.Eventually, Delhi gave us newer places to hang out. Aerocity emerged as a nightlife and dining destination and there was a resurgence of Delhi’s OG hangout spot – Connaught Place. Greater Kailash I and II, Meherchand Market and Mehrauli also started giving us enough reasons to explore beyond HKV.And all those who witnessed HKV in its prime also witnessed its downfall. Just for the sake of reliving the good times, some of us who used to be regulars revisited the place, only to be disappointed by the run-down bars and ushers screaming “one plus one” and “live music” to lure the few people passing by. For a place where finding space to walk on a weekend was once difficult, seeing those empty lanes was almost unbelievable.Perhaps that’s also why the downfall of HKV hits Delhi millennials differently. This wasn’t just another market where restaurants opened and shut. This was where many of us spent our weekends, celebrated birthdays, met friends, discovered new cafes, danced till late and, at some point, knew the lanes well enough to have our own favourite spots.Now, we hear that after the gradual downfall of Delhi’s once-affluent hipster village, neighbouring G Block Market is on its way to attaining a certain status as a restaurant hub. We can’t help but wonder: Can the area revive the glory of HKV?And even if it does, will it ever mean the same thing to those of us who remember a time when saying, “HKV chalte hain?” was enough of a weekend plan?
Article Summary: Hauz Khas Village of the late ’90s and early 2000s had this unique blend of affordable and aspirational that made it appealing to youngsters. For millennials, weekends would often mean heading to HKV, and there was a certain kind of pride worth flaunting if you knew all the new places there.

Article Title: CJP leaders Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka attempt to breach Jantar Mantar 2 days after release under 1-year ‘maintain peace’ condition: 'You cannot denotify resistance, PM Modi'
Article Text:
CJP leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were detained by Delhi Police on Tuesday





NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were detained by Delhi Police on Tuesday while attempting to reach Jantar Mantar just two days after they were released by an executive magistrate on the condition that they 'maintain peace' and 'good behaviour' for a year.The fresh detentions came after the leaders were released on Sunday following their preventive arrest ahead of a protest demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in voter rolls.The Delhi Police had said the leaders were released by the Special Executive Magistrate (SEM) Court, Delhi Cantt, after a surety bond of Rs 50,000 was furnished."A bail bond as surety bond of Rs 50,000 was filed for maintaining peace and good behaviour, for a period of one year, and they were released by the SEM Court," the police said on Sunday.CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke said several other party members, including Ajinkya Shinde, had also been detained on Tuesday.In a post on X, Dipke said, "Cockroaches with the Tiranga sneaked into Jantar Mantar early this morning before they were picked up by Delhi Police. AshutoshRanka, Saurav Das and Ajinkya along with other team members have been detained. You cannot denotify the resistance, Narendra Modi."Despite the detentions, CJP members described their attempt to enter the protest site as a success and renewed their call for Kumar's resignation.In a post on X, Das said, "Jantar Mantar has been reclaimed. We have entered Jantar Mantar and now we are being detained. But this is a message to all of us young gen! We can do it! Gyanu, you’re done bro!"Ranka also posted on X, "Fortress Jantar Mantar has been breached."Dipke shared a picture of Ranka waving the Tricolour at the site, while Ranka posted, "Hands Off Jantar Mantar."The party members had gathered at Jantar Mantar in the early hours of Tuesday. Security personnel arrived shortly after the demonstration began and detained protesters who attempted to enter the venue after it had been denotified as a protest site.
Article Summary: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were detained by Delhi Police on Tuesday. The fresh detentions came after the leaders were released on Sunday following their preventive arrest. CJP members described their attempt to enter the protest site as a success and renewed their call for Kumar's resignation.

Article Title: As MPSC stir ends, 1st big victory for student-led protests
Article Text:
1st big victory for student-led protests

Mumbai:

2nd MPSC chief to face action in 24 years





Govt’s decision to send MPSC chairperson Vivek Bhimanwar on leave till completion of a judicial inquiry into alleged exam irregularities is a major victory for student-led protests in the state in recent times.So far, the state govt had tried to pacify agitators through govt resolutions, formation of inquiry committees and announcement of new policy measures.Political observers said what forced govt to blink this time was the protests’ national visibility—the participation of hundreds of students, the backing of NCP (SP) MLA Rohit Pawar , MNS chief Raj Thackeray and other state opposition netas, the repeated endorsement by Congress MP Rahul Gandhi through a flurry of social media posts, and the appearance of an array of activists like CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke and folk singer Neha Singh Rathore at the agitation sites.Amid massive ongoing protests against alleged electoral fraud, the state govt was keen to defuse the MPSC protests before they snowballed further, said officials.They said CM Devendra Fadnavis also pulled off a balancing act by appointing FDA chief Tukaram Mundhe as the secretary of the inquiry panel before sending Bhimanwar on leave. “This was a masterstroke given the pressure being created by student protests. By getting Mundhe in the inquiry committee, Fadnavis scored on the perception front and made it clear that it would be a fair inquiry.So, when Bhimanwar went on leave instead of resigning, it looked like a middle ground had been reached,” said a senior official.A political observer said the MPSC protests became a rallying point for netas from all opposition parties. “They also helped Rohit establish himself as a seasoned opposition neta, one who is consistently batting for student issues. His jugalbandi with Rahul was also noticed and that compelled a lot of Congress netas to join and express support.”This is the second such instance of an MPSC chief facing govt action in 24 years. ACB arrested then chairperson Shashikant Karnik in 2002 over an alleged multi-crore recruitment fraud. He later resigned. A disproportionate assets case was filed in 2005 and a court discharged him in 2009. A former MPSC member said the commission had a largely unblemished record from then till the current controversy broke out.
Article Summary: MPSC chairperson Vivek Bhimanwar on leave till completion of a judicial inquiry into alleged exam irregularities. This is the second such instance of an MPSC chief facing govt action in 24 years. ACB arrested then chairperson Shashikant Karnik in 2002 over an alleged multi-crore recruitment fraud. He later resigned.

Article Title: Barricade row sparks temple fracas as devotees fume over Mahalaxmi Navaratra arrangements
Article Text:
A heated arguement broke out between the Shripujaks, Paschim Maharashtra Devasthan Samiti and the police at Mahalaxmi temple on Monday, the second day of Navratra

Kolhapur

:





A row over crowd management at Kolhapur’s Mahalaxmi temple erupted into a public fracas on Monday, with priests, temple authorities and police clashing over barricading and movement restrictions that devotees say have turned a revered pilgrimage into an ordeal.The confrontation broke out on the second day of Navaratra when Shripujaks (priests) accused the administration of interfering in religious practices and insulting them by obstructing temple rituals. The protest inside the temple premises briefly disrupted the otherwise festive atmosphere.Since Navaratra began, devotees and priests have been voicing anger over altered entry and exit routes and extensive barricading put in place by police. Instead of easing movement, the measures have triggered confusion, longer queues and growing resentment among devotees.“The Mukhdarshan route, which was convenient every year, has been made complicated this Navaratra. The waiting time, which earlier used to be around 15 to 20 minutes, has increased to nearly an hour,” said devotee Smita Patil from Mangalwar Peth.Devotees also complained about poor facilities along the queues.Patil said there was no matting on parts of the Pradakshina route, forcing devotees to walk on hot surfaces, while shade arrangements on the Mukhdarshan queue were inadequate.Tempers flared further on Monday afternoon when members of Hindu outfits objected to barricades erected inside the temple precincts. Heated arguments followed as protesters questioned the need for the restrictions and accused authorities of making darshan unnecessarily difficult.“The administration claims there is coordination between the authorities, the Devasthan Samiti and the police, but it has forgotten the connection between devotees and the goddess. Lakhs of devotees visit the Mahalaxmi temple every year with deep faith. This time, the barricading makes the temple premises look like an international border, with devotees being treated like terrorists,” a protester said.The protesters warned that if the barricades were not removed, they would take matters into their own hands and dismantle them from Tuesday. The episode exposed growing cracks in coordination between Paschim Maharashtra Devasthan Samiti, police and temple stakeholders at a time when lakhs of devotees are expected during the nine-day festival.Despite the controversy, the flow of devotees remained unabated. Temple authorities recorded 1,19,205 devotees on Monday alone.The goddess was adorned in the revered Sarvasyada Mahalaxmi form, with ritual worship performed by priests Ajinkya Munishwar, Vedang Munishwar, Soham Munishwar and Ravi Mainkar. But outside the sanctum, the focus remained firmly on the crowd-control measures that turned a day of devotion into a day of confrontation.
Article Summary: Priests, authorities and police clash at Mahalaxmi temple on second day of Navaratra. Shripujaks (priests) accuse administration of interfering in religious practices. Protesters question need for restrictions and accuse authorities of making darshan unnecessarily difficult.

Article Title: 3 devotees die in 2 accidents
Article Text:
Kolhapur

:





Three devotees died in two separate accidents while carrying a flambeau (jyot) from Tuljapur to their villages.Sambhaji Prahlad Kadam (40) and Rajesh Appasaheb Kadam (38) were among a group of 17 people from Kouthali village in Atpadi taluka of Sangli district, who had travelled to Tuljapur to bring the jyot. The flame is kept burning at their village pandal throughout the nine days of Navaratra.On Sunday morning, while returning along Tuljapur-Dharashiv Road at Tuljainagar, a goods carrier vehicle hit the two-wheeler they were riding on. They were rushed to hospital, but were declared brought dead. Other devotees returned to the village with their bodies.In the second case, 45-year-old Prakash Jagganath Dighe from Wadegaon in Sangola taluka of Solapur district was run over by an unknown vehicle. The accident took place around 4.30 pm on Sunday along Sangola-Mangalwedha road.During Navaratra, devotees traditionally bring a flame from Shaktipeeths, such as Mahalaxmi in Kolhapur, where the goddess is the main deity. They leave days before the festival begins and carry the flame while running barefoot, exchanging it after covering a certain distance.Other participants follow on motorbikes and in a carrier vehicle, cooking and eating along the roadside during the journey.
Article Summary: Sambhaji Prahlad Kadam, Rajesh Appasaheb Kadam and Prakash Jagganath Dighe died. They were among 17 people who had travelled to Tuljapur to bring the jyot. The flame is kept burning at their village pandal throughout Navaratra.

Article Title: Days before her wedding, engineering student found dead in Maharashtra gorge, boyfriend held
Article Text:
Naikwadi waterfall of Bhudargad





KOLHAPUR: A 25-year-old man has been arrested on suspicion of murdering his 23-year-old girlfriend, an engineering student whose body was found nearly 1,000ft below a cliff at Naikwadi waterfalls Maharashtra's Kolhapur.Police came to know of the death Saturday when Sripad Vadar walked into a PS and reported that Tarrannum Naik, a third-year student who lived with her maternal grandmother in Gargoti, had fallen into a gorge from a cliff.Police sent a team to the remote site and retrieved her body."He told us they had been in a relationship for five-and-a-half years and were distressed because her family had fixed her marriage elsewhere. According to him, the couple had decided to die by suicide together. He claimed she jumped into the gorge, but he lost his nerve at the last moment," sub-divisional police officer Vivek Patil said.Naikwadi waterfalls are deep inside forested terrain, about 50km from Gargoti. The falls were dry after the monsoon, and no visitors were in the area when the couple reached the spot Friday, police said.Police registered a case under section 140(3) of BNS, relating to wrongful confinement.But examination of messages exchanged between the couple raised doubts about Sripad's account."The chat history does not support the account he gave us about a suicide pact. The messages suggested Sripad was upset over Tarrannum's family's decision to get her married to someone else. That raised serious doubts and led us to invoke BNS section 103(1) for murder," Patil said.Accused Sripad, also from Gargoti, worked with his brother, a local contractor. On Sunday, a court remanded Sripad in police custody for five days.Police have seized mobile phones of both Tarrannum and the accused for forensic analysis. Police are awaiting the autopsy report.Tarrannum's last rites were performed at her native Patgaon. Her marriage had been fixed for Nov 12. Her death sparked protests in Gargoti, where residents marched to police station Sunday and demanded a fast-track trial.
Article Summary: Tarrannum Naik, 23, was found dead at Naikwadi waterfalls in Kolhapur, Maharashtra. Her boyfriend Sripad Vadar, 25, has been arrested on suspicion of murder. He told police the couple had decided to die by suicide together. Her death sparked protests in Gargoti, where residents marched to police station.

Article Title: Mumbai-bound traffic hit after hatchback catches fire on Vashi Creek bridge
Article Text:
The driver immediately pulled the car over to the roadside after noticing smoke emanating from the engine.





NAVI MUMBAI: Vehicular traffic from Navi Mumbai towards Mumbai was disrupted for around 30 minutes after a hatchback caught fire while crossing the Vashi Creek Bridge on Friday at around 7.30pm.The driver escaped unhurt. He immediately pulled the car over to the roadside after noticing smoke emanating from the engine. However, the fire soon engulfed the entire vehicle, leaving it completely charred.Vashi traffic police alerted the Vashi fire brigade, which reached the spot within 15 minutes. The charred vehicle was later towed away by a crane, following which traffic movement returned to normal.Sunil Kadam, senior inspector of the Vashi traffic unit, said the driver was identified as Sumit Bhikaji Kadam.“At around 7.45pm, we received a call from one Rahul, whose full name is not known, informing us that a car had caught fire on the Mumbai-bound lane of the Vashi Creek Bridge,” said AV Sisode, the on-duty fireman at Vashi fire station.“In the meantime, we also received a call from the Vashi traffic police and immediately rushed to the spot with a fire tender. The Mumbai fire brigade team had also reached the spot as there was some confusion over the jurisdiction,” Sisode said.The fire was subsequently extinguished, and the Vashi fire brigade team returned to the station at around 8.30pm.
Article Summary: The driver immediately pulled the car over to the roadside after noticing smoke emanating from the engine. The fire soon engulfed the entire vehicle, leaving it completely charred. The charred vehicle was later towed away by a crane, following which traffic movement returned to normal.

Article Title: Mumbai-Goa highway crash: 30-year-old killed, 2 cousins injured after Honda City hits gate
Article Text:
30-year-old Akshay Kadam lost his life in a car accident after he lost control of his vehicle





NAVI MUMBAI: A 30-year-old man driving his Honda City car was killed and his two friends, both paternal cousin brothers accompanying him were injured after the driver lost control over the wheels on the Mangaon-Mahad stretch of Mumbai-Goa highway after crossing Mangaon railway station and veering off the road crashed into the iron gate of an industrial unit.The fatal accident occured on Monday around 3 am, when the three friends had gone for dinner at a roadside food stall in Mangaon and were returning to their respective villages in Mahad taluka.The injured complainant stated in the FIR registered at Mangaon police station that the accused car driver and his cousin had consumed liquor before going for dinner.The deceased driver was identified as Akshay Arjun Kadam, a resident of Nandgaon, Mahad taluka. Those injured are Rohit Rajendra Dhadve (24), working as safety officer at Astriel Life Science Pvt Ltd in Mahad MIDC and his cousin Roshan Dilip Dhadve (24). Both residents of Kembhurli, Mahad taluka.Maruti Andhale, senior inspector of Mangaon said, "As the complainant Rohit Dhadve has stated in the FIR that the accused Akshay Kadam drove the car after consuming liquor along with his cousin Roshan, when they had meet near the bus stop, after which they went to Mangaon for dinner, the Motor Vehicle Act section for drunk driving will be invoked.However, as the accused car driver Akshay Kadam responsible for the car crash had died in the accident, a final closure 'Abated summary' report will be submitted before the Mangaon magistrate court. "As per the FIR by the complainant Rohit Dhadve, on Sept 28 around 1 am, when he was at home, his paternal cousin Roshan spoke to him over mobile, when Roshan's maternal cousin Akshay Kadam accompanying him told Rohit that he had come from Mumbai and asked him to meet near the bus stand at Kembhurli.When Rohit met them at the spot, Roshan and Akshay were consuming liquor inside Akshay's Honda City car. Thereafter, Akshay said, "Let's go to Mangaon to have food and the three of them went in the car with Akshay at the wheels."Roshan was sitting beside Akshay and Rohit on the rear seat. They reached Mangaon around 2 am, where they ate parathas at a road side food stall and took parcel of Khima Pav.Thereafter, they drove for 3 kms towards Indapur and took a U-turn to return to their villages in Mahad.After crossing 300 metres from Mangaon railway Station, Akshay lost control over the wheels and yanking off the road on the right side, he crashed into the iron gate of Sundha Steel Traders industrial unit.Rohit sustained injuries below his left eye, left hand and left knee. Akshay got stuck between the driver's seat and the door. Roshan's left leg was injured.Hearing the loud noice of the car crash, the locals gathered, removed the three injured out of the car and summoned 108 ambulance in which they were rushed to Mangaon sub-district hospital, where Akshay was declared brought dead on arrival.
Article Summary: Akshay Arjun Kadam, 30, lost his life in a car accident after he lost control of his vehicle on the Mumbai-Goa highway. His two friends, both paternal cousin brothers accompanying him were injured. The three friends had gone for dinner at a roadside food stall in Mangaon.

Article Title: Nagpur University Misses Convocation Date Again
Article Text:
Nagpur:





For the second consecutive time, Nagpur University (NU) has failed to hold its convocation as scheduled. The university’s academic calendar, issued at the beginning of the year, had earmarked Oct 11 for the degree-awarding ceremony, but the date passed without the event taking place.Sources said no confirmed date has been announced for the convocation covering the winter 2025 and summer 2026 examinations.The university had also failed to hold its convocation on time earlier, with the ceremony repeatedly postponed for administrative reasons and the absence of a full-time vice-chancellor. It was eventually held in Jan 2026.NU has three important dates on its annual calendar: Aug 4, its foundation day; April 30, the birth anniversary of Rashtrasant Tukadoji Maharaj, after whom the university is named; and Oct 11, his death anniversary.Sources said April is considered too late for the convocation, while August is generally too early, as the university is still processing examination results and revaluation applications. Oct is considered a more suitable window, allowing the examination cycle to progress before degrees are awarded. NU had accordingly scheduled the ceremony for Oct 11.The delay contrasts with Visvesvaraya National Institute of Technology (VNIT), which holds its convocation on Sept 15 every year to pay tribute to Sir M Visvesvaraya, after whom the institute is named.NU officials, meanwhile, said convocation dates in the academic calendar were tentative and subject to approval from Governor’s office. Approval for the latest ceremony is still awaited, they said, adding that preparation of the merit list is underway.However, the academic calendar does not explicitly state that the Oct 11 date is subject to approval from Governor’s office.
Article Summary: Nagpur University (NU) has failed to hold its convocation as scheduled. The university's academic calendar had earmarked Oct 11 for the degree-awarding ceremony. No confirmed date has been announced for the convocation covering the winter 2025 and summer 2026 examinations.

Article Title: AI levels the playing field for entrepreneurs from Chennai: Mithun Sacheti
Article Text:
Mithun Sacheti, founder, CaratLane & partner at Q Partners - Axana Estates at the event

Chennai:





AI levels the playing field for entrepreneurs building out of Chennai by solving the infrastructure advantage traditionally held by major hubs like Mumbai and Delhi, said Mithun Sacheti, founder of CaratLane and Partner at Q Partners- Axana Estates.Speaking at the Madras Management Association (MMA) management students’ convention 2026, he said being in a relatively quiet place allows entrepreneurs to build without distraction, while AI bridges the talent gaps as it makes possible to get the work done with a smaller teams. “AI is the biggest game changer that has happened in my entrepreneurship journey... It solves the infrastructure layer that gave Mumbai, Delhi an advantage. We have all the information that anybody else has anywhere else. For jobs now you do not need so many people, and your own capacity multiplies by 10 times,” he added.Wide range of speakers and panellists, including notable startup founders examined the realities of moving from campus to startup, transforming organisations in an AI-driven world, building future-ready careers and leading adaptively through change and uncertainty.The session concluded with the presentation of awards to the winners of Chanakya, the Mastermind and the other management competitions held as part of the convention.
Article Summary: Mithun Sacheti, founder of CaratLane, spoke at the Madras Management Association (MMA) management students’ convention 2026. He said being in a relatively quiet place allows entrepreneurs to build without distraction, while AI bridges the talent gaps.
